title: IN-F5: Adapting an English TTS Foundation Model for Multilingual and Zero-Resource Indian Speech Synthesis
abstract: We investigate whether an English TTS foundation model (F5-TTS) can serve as an effective prior for low-resource multilingual speech synthesis. Starting from an English-pretrained checkpoint, we adapt to 11 Indian languages using less than 2% of the original pretraining data scale. Through a controlled comparison of training from scratch, direct fine-tuning, and fine-tuning with continued English exposure, we find that direct fine-tuning on Indian data alone performs best, challenging the assumption that multilingual systems benefit from continued high-resource exposure. Extensive subjective and objective evaluations show that the resulting model, IN-F5, approaches human-level naturalness and speaker similarity while exhibiting emergent capabilities including polyglot voice transfer, code-mixing, and expressive style control. We analyze data scaling and demonstrate zero-resource cross-lingual transfer to Bhojpuri and Tulu to extend TTS to under-represented languages.
relevance_note: IN-F5, adapting English F5-TTS to 11 Indian languages including zero-resource settings; multilingual TTS method.
